task.title: Report HTTP 403 and 429 links as blocked, not as broken internal links
task.body:
Why: packages/seo/docs/research/handoff-audit-unlighthouse-quality-2026-10-07.md:193 ("403/429 probe nie dowodzi dead link"); packages/seo/src/domain/findings.ts:155 emits `broken-internal-link` for every status >= 400.
Outcome: `buildFindings(pages)` (src/domain/findings.ts) no longer emits `broken-internal-link` for a page whose `status` is 403 or 429. For such a page it emits exactly one finding with `ruleId` `"link-probe-blocked"`, `url` equal to the page url, and `evidence` containing the string `"Target returned HTTP <status>."` (e.g. `"Target returned HTTP 429."`), plus the existing `"Observed same-origin link from <source>."` lines for each linking source. Every other status >= 400 (404, 410, 500, 503, ...) still yields `broken-internal-link` exactly as before, and no `link-probe-blocked` finding. `link-probe-blocked` must be registered as a known rule id (catalog, playbook and documented inventories).
Proof: registering the rule means the existing consistency suites must stay green: packages/seo/src/domain/rule-catalog.ts, rule-playbook.ts, docs/audit-coverage.md (rule count and register row) and references/check-catalog.md (rule count and row) all gain the new id. The implementer adds own tests in tests/domain/findings.test.ts for 403, 429 and an unchanged 404, and runs the rule-catalog suite.
